widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is <Picture 1> Pixel Dusk from the first character reference sheet: shoulder-length wavy dark purple hair, glowing purple eyes, black cropped jacket with purple stitching over a tight purple tank top, black tactical pants with purple side stripes, black fingerless gloves, purple-black sneakers, and the silver grapnel cane with purple wrapping (both extended and collapsed forms). The purple media visor is part of her design.
<Subject 2> is <Picture 2> Jaro Venn from the second character reference sheet: slick black hair with precise side part, strong defined jawline, warm tan skin, confident expression, brown eyes, iridescent shiny purple high-collar suit with structured shoulders and long coat tails, silver metallic vertical strips on the lapels and vest, white dress shirt, and black gloves. His signature prop is the set of blank white key-cards with thin purple edges.
<Subject 3> is <Picture 3> the Crownwell city environment taken from the establishing reference images: the massive central circular cyan energy vortex, towering white-and-purple skyscrapers, elevated walkways, neon signage, reflective metallic surfaces, and the overall high-tech plaza layout under mixed daylight and neon lighting.

summary:
[reference generation] A 5-second high-energy action sequence in Crownwell. <Subject 1> (Pixel Dusk) swings into the central plaza on her grapnel cane, lands, activates her media visor, and engages <Subject 2> (Jaro Venn), who deploys holographic shields from his key-cards. The environment (<Subject 3>) remains consistent throughout. Fast cuts, dynamic camera angles, and strong motion inspired by Riot Worlds cinematic style.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in all shots): fully_preserved - exact appearance, clothing, proportions, hair, eye color, and props from the character sheet are maintained with no redesign.
<Subject 2> (appears from Shot 4 onward): fully_preserved - exact face, hair, skin tone, suit design, silver accents, and key-card prop from the character sheet are maintained with no redesign.
<Subject 3> (background in all shots): fully_preserved - the central cyan vortex, architecture, color palette, and plaza layout from the establishing references are kept consistent.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] High-detail 2D digital illustration matching the clean cel-shaded style of the character reference sheets. Extreme wide high-angle shot of Crownwell (<Subject 3>) with the glowing cyan energy vortex at the center of the plaza. <Subject 1> swings in on the fully extended grapnel cane from a high building, body arched, purple energy trailing along the cable.
[Shot 2] At 00:00.800, the camera cuts to a dynamic low-angle medium tracking shot on a reflective metallic walkway. <Subject 1> lands hard, knees bent, the grapnel cane collapsing into its short baton form while the purple media visor flips down over her eyes with a bright glow. She holds a ready, forward-leaning stance.
[Shot 3] At 00:01.600, the camera cuts to an extreme close-up of <Subject 1>’s face. The media visor is fully engaged, glowing purple lenses framing her intense purple eyes. Soft hair movement and neon reflections slide across the visor surface.
[Shot 4] At 00:02.400, the camera cuts to a medium 3/4 view of <Subject 2> standing in the plaza with the cyan vortex visible behind him. He turns sharply, raising a fan of blank key-cards that begin emitting soft holographic purple light.
[Shot 5] At 00:03.200, the camera cuts to a fast side-angle tracking shot of the confrontation. <Subject 1> swings the re-extended grapnel cane in a powerful arc with purple energy trails and motion blur. <Subject 2> raises the key-cards, which expand into large translucent holographic purple geometric shields.
[Shot 6] At 00:04.100, the camera cuts to a high-angle Dutch-tilt impact frame. The tip of the grapnel cane collides with the holographic shields in a bright purple-cyan energy explosion with sparks and particles. Both characters recoil slightly while the Crownwell vortex pulses brighter in the background.

overall_soundscape: Distant city hum mixed with the low-frequency energy drone of the central vortex. Metallic whoosh and cable snap of the grapnel, hard boot impact on metal plating, soft fabric movement, rising holographic energy crackle, and a sharp high-frequency clash at the final impact.

non_diegetic_music: Fast-tempo electronic track with driving distorted bass, sharp synth stabs locked to the cuts, rising filtered noise risers into the clash, and a short aggressive low-end punch on the final impact before a quick cutoff.

nodes.title: READ ME - LTX-2.5 2x
widgets_values:
LTX-2.5 LATENT SPATIAL x2 (24GB-safe)
Kept the cheap official latent spatial x2 path. The MBEDIT vrs6 'better' LTX upscaler is a 22B distilled v2v refine after RTX (not resize) at ~3MP. That recipe ran on a 12GB 3060, but it needs ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors which is not in this library (only the video VAE is). Enabling a half-wired 22B path would just error, so it is not swapped in here.

What WAS applied from that repo: H3 dual sampler with RTX x1.5 between passes (the higher-quality upscale). Use Studio's LTX-2.5 toggle for this latent x2, and RTX SVU for a final pixel upscale.

Models for this path:
  latent_upscale_models/ltx/ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-bf16-1.0.safetensors
  vae/ltx-2.5/ltx-2.5-video-vae-conv-bf16.safetensors

nodes.title: READ ME - Post Grade
widgets_values:
POST GRADE + PIPELINE FIXES (v4)
Created using Anthropic Claude - keep this note on internal versions
until the settings have been reviewed/verified.

PATH:
  VAEDecode -> LTX-2.5 latent spatial x2 -> Grade
    -> Interpolation -> Sharpen -> VideoCombine
LTX must stay before interpolation.

The grade used to sit after interpolation, so it processed every
interpolated frame (124 -> 616 with RIFE alone, ~4900 with all three
stacked). It now runs on the 124 decoded frames. The last-frame save
for shot chaining is also taken post-grade, so the next shot starts
from a colour-matched frame.

ONE INTERPOLATOR AT A TIME. They chain in series, so enabling two
multiplies: RIFE 5x * GMFSS 4x * FILM 2x = 40x the frames and an
8x audio/video desync. v3 shipped with all three live - that was
the performance collapse. The parent "Frame Interpolation" group
was deleted because toggling it re-enabled all three at once; the
three child groups are now brown and appear in the main toggler,
with "max one" enforced by the small bypasser next to them.

FPS and frames share the same switch order (first live wins):
  any_01 GMFSS   96  (4x). Unused interpolators must be MUTED, not bypassed.
  any_02 FILM    48  (2x). Bypass passes original frames through and a 96fps
  any_03 RIFE   120  (5x). file of those frames plays in ~1s.
  any_04 original / base 24
Change a multiplier -> change the matching fps primitive.

RIFE flow scale is 1.0. It was 4.0, which computes optical flow at
4x resolution for roughly 16x the cost with no benefit at 544p.
Try 2.0 if you want more accurate flow and can pay for it.

Grade is still BYPASSED and lut_file is "None" - nothing is being
graded right now. Enable the Post Grade group and pick
Worlds_AMV_Style.cube to get the look back.

Output is h264 / yuv420p 8-bit / crf 16. For the HDR grade, enable
the Master Export (h265, yuv420p10le, crf 12) instead - 8-bit will
band the shadow rolloff.

GRADE TUNING (change one at a time):
 1 Pseudo-HDR  hdr_intensity 0.45. Above ~0.8 goes haloed.
 2 LUT         strength 0.7. 0.4-0.5 if skin goes too gold.
 3 Trim        saturation/contrast +10-15 finishing pass.
 4 Bloom       intensity 0; most memory-hungry stage here.
 5 Sharpen     alpha 0.35 subtle, 0.6+ crunchy. Stays after the
               upscaler so it works at final resolution.

Requires Worlds_AMV_Style.cube in ComfyUI/models/luts/ and
colour-science in python_embeded. The LUT is an algorithmic
approximation of the Riot Worlds look, not an official Riot asset.

nodes.title: Dual Sampler (from MBEDIT MH3 v12)
widgets_values: H3 dual sampler at native res: pass 1 and pass 2 share the Sampler subgraph (euler + Spectrum + LowVRAM + Chunk FF=2). Pass 2 refines the pass 1 latent (Studio pass2 steps / denoise / scheduler / sampler / shift). No RTX between passes — LTX/RTX stay on the post path only. Guides stay (canvas is unchanged). Pass 1 audio is kept. Turn off Studio DUAL PASS to mute this group (single pass). Do not bypass it: the PASS 2 Sampler subgraph would leak MODEL into GetImageSize. Lipsync: keep pass 2 denoise at or below 0.3. pass2_scale is unused.
